subject: FinoLabs: regression after model v2.7-quant deployment — urgent
messages:
From: Asha Verma <support@finolabs.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: 2026-02-14T09:12:45-08:00
Subject: Unexpected latency + hallucination spike after model push

Aditya —

We pushed the new model bundle (v2.7-quant8) in our staging->prod pipeline yesterday evening and immediately started seeing elevated latencies and a quality regression. Quick summary from our side (production traffic):
- P95 latency: ~220ms -> ~520ms since the push (median up ~1.6x)
- Error/timeouts: increased from ~0.3% to ~5% over the last 3 hours
- Throughput: sustained throughput dropped ~28% under the same traffic profile
- Quality: automated eval on 1k QA prompts flagged a 12% increase in hallucination-like responses (examples attached)

We rolled back on our side as a stopgap but customers saw degraded behavior for ~40 minutes. We believe this change is tied to the quant profile in the new variant, but we need Redwood to confirm whether the uploaded quant profile or runtime selection caused a fallback or slower kernel selection. We need an urgent RCA and a mitigation plan before we re-run the upgrade.

I attached a small sample response set and a p95 snapshot. Can someone from your infra/run team pick this up? Our C-suite is asking for a timeline for a technical explanation and for potential customer remediation (credits/notice).

Thanks —
Asha Verma
Head of ML Systems, FinoLabs
support@finolabs.com

Attachments:
- finolabs_sample_response_set.json
- p95_latency_screens.png

Subject: Fwd: Unexpected latency + hallucination spike after model push

Looping Monica for infra + quant profile triage; Vivek since this needs exec visibility.

Asha — thanks for the quick report and attachments. Monica, can you triage the following ASAP:
- Confirm whether v2.7-quant8 triggered any host fallback or slower kernel path (CPU fallback / attention kernel mismatch).
- Check routing: was FinoLabs routed to a different instance class (older drivers / different cudnn)?
- Compare KV cache behavior and prefix caching between v2.6 and v2.7 bundles.

If we confirm a runtime regression, we'll plan an immediate rollback of the deployed variant and prepare a post-mortem for the customer. Vivek — FYI, customer is a mid-enterprise account (DL-9876) with an upcoming renewal; they asked about credits.

I will keep Asha updated with ETA and next steps.

—Aditya Rao

From: monica_patel@redwood.com
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: Asha Verma <support@finolabs.com>
Date: 2026-02-14T10:10:02-08:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Unexpected latency + hallucination spike after model push

Aditya / Vivek / Asha — quick triage notes after an initial look at the traces and perf matrices (attached):
- Root cause hypothesis: quantization profile shipped with v2.7 triggered a mixed-kernel execution path on some GPU hosts. We observed repeated small kernel fallbacks (attention scratch allocations) that inflates per-token latency.
- Secondary issue: on a subset of hosts the new binary combination disables a fast-path for KV cache pinning (config flag mismatch), which increases memory churn and causes GC-like stalls under burst traffic.
- Impact: both mechanisms explain the p95 spike and throughput drop; the hallucination increase is likely due to a subtle numeric shift from the quant profile (low-bit rounding) for some prompt templates.

Immediate recommended actions (30–90m window):
1) Initiate targeted rollback for FinoLabs to v2.6 (non-quant or v2.6q) across their routed pool to restore baseline latency.
2) Produce a patched quant profile and a new runtime flag to re-enable KV cache pinning path; run A/B on a small % of traffic after validation.
3) Run deterministic unit tests on the 400 QA prompts Asha shared to measure delta and confirm if hallucination drop is reversible via quant tweak.

I've attached: trace_v2.7_span.log and perf_matrix.csv for the affected hosts. We'll start packaging a hotfix branch and run perf regressions locally; I'll post a link to test results in the ticket.

—Monica Patel
Lead SRE, Inference Runtime
monica_patel@redwood.com
Attachments:
- trace_v2.7_span.log
- perf_matrix.csv

Asha / Rajat —

Thank you for surfacing this and for the artifacts — we've validated an initial hypothesis internally and will take these steps immediately:
- Start a rollback to v2.6 for FinoLabs' routed pool now. Target completion: ~90 minutes from now.
- Run the A/B harness on the patched quant profile in a controlled environment before any re-roll.
- Monica's team will deliver a preliminary RCA and perf artifact within 48 hours; a full post-mortem with remediation plan in 7 business days.

Customer remediation: after rollback completes we'll propose a one-time credit; I'll coordinate with finance and legal and loop back with a formal offer for your review.

Links: JIRA INF-4521 (investigation), log bundle (S3) — I'll update the ticket with traces and the rollback timeline.

We're sorry for the disruption. I will send live updates as rollback progresses.

—Aditya Rao

Subject: Executive summary: FinoLabs regression, rollback, and remediation proposal

Vivek — final exec summary for the record and to request approval for the proposed customer remediation:
- Timeline: Regression reported 2026-02-14 09:12 PST; immediate rollback executed 2026-02-14 10:50 PST; affected window ~40 minutes (some customers observed degraded results).
- Root cause: quant profile + runtime kernel selection mismatch on a subset of GPU hosts; secondary KV cache pinning flag bug amplified latency under burst. Monica's team validated the root cause and produced a patched quant profile.
- Impact: p95 latency increase to ~520ms for routed traffic and a 12% uptick in hallucination flags on our 1k-sample test set. No data leakage or integrity violation found.
- Customer remediation request: FinoLabs asked about credits. Recommended offer: 30% credit for the affected window on next invoice + 2 incident response hours waived for remediation validation.
- Next steps: get exec sign-off on credits, finalize postmortem doc (attached draft), and schedule a 1-hour RCA session with Fino execs next week.

Please confirm if we should move forward with the proposed credit and the timing for the RCA session. If yes, I'll run the formal credit through Finance and prepare the customer comms.

—Aditya Rao
aditya_rao@redwood.com
